intent: The archive confirmation gets the product's standard shell, and its three messages stop wearing the same anonymous border: the consequence speaks in the consequence role, a bounced attempt speaks in danger, a refusal to mint speaks in notice.
rationale: Today every message block on this page is 'rounded border p-N text-sm' — the platform's consequence sentence, a failed attempt's reason, and the cannot-archive refusal are visually one thing, distinguishable only by reading. DT-0001 built the semantic roles exactly for this (quiet/notice/consequence), and DT-0002 ruled where the weight belongs on a confirmation: never on the button, always on the consequence block. This ticket extends both rulings to the archive page unchanged: the button stays un-dangered per the manifest constraint and spec 'present archiving as recoverable' (agent-authoring spec.md:202) — but the *problem* banner is not advisory and not the legitimate action; it reports a write the platform refused, and it takes danger.subtle so a bounced attempt cannot be skimmed past as one more bordered paragraph. The secondary button also gains its first hover treatment: an anchor that changes nothing on pointer-over reads as inert text in a box.

design.layout: Standard confirmation shell exactly as DT-0001's implementation landed it: centred column (stock max-w-2xl), space.5 page padding, vertical rhythm space.4 between blocks, heading at type.size.xl / type.weight.medium. Identical shell in every state, including not-connected and refused.

proposal.content: Shell + heading 'Archive <name>?', consequence block, button row. The consequence block is the visually heaviest element between heading and buttons: color.consequence.subtle background, 1px color.consequence.border border, radius.2, space.4 padding, body text at type.size.sm / color.text.primary. role=alert stays. The platform's sentence renders verbatim — no truncation, no paraphrase.

proposal-with-problem.content: Same as proposal with the problem banner first, above the consequence block, in the reading order the redirect put it: what you tried failed, here is what archiving still means, here are the buttons. The two blocks must not share a palette role — problem is danger.subtle, consequence is consequence.subtle.

refused.content: Shell + heading 'Cannot archive' + the platform's reason in a notice block: color.notice.subtle background, 1px color.notice.border border, radius.2, space.4 padding, color.text.primary text, role=alert kept. No form beneath, no dismiss control, nothing styled as disabled — the refusal explains, per DT-0001's vocabulary-unavailable treatment.

not-connected.content: Rendered by the shared not-connected component. This ticket guarantees only that it inherits the same shell; its own treatment is out of scope here — it is shared by every page and deserves its own ticket.

present.content: The problem banner: color.danger.subtle background, 1px color.danger.default border, radius.2, space.4 padding, type.size.sm text in color.text.primary. role=alert stays. Not color-alone: it opens with the bolded word 'Refused:' at type.weight.semibold before the platform's reason, so the state is named as well as tinted.

absent.content: Nothing renders and no space is reserved — the consequence block sits directly under the heading.

default.content: Buttons as DT-0002 landed them: primary on color.accent.default with color.accent.text, secondary as a color.border.default bordered peer; both at min-height size.control.min, radius from the shared constants. The button row is flex with space.3 gap and wraps.

hover.content: Primary: color.accent.hover background over motion.duration.fast (unchanged). Secondary, new: border shifts to color.border.strong and background to color.bg.sunken over motion.duration.fast — enough to say 'this is a control', not enough to compete with primary.

focused.content: The global focus-visible ring (2px, color.focus) — no per-element ring is added, per the manifest constraint.

active.content: Primary: holds color.accent.hover with transition at motion.duration.instant — a press reads as immediate, not animated. Secondary: holds its hover treatment the same way. No transform, no layout shift.

responsive.mobile: Buttons stretch full width and stack in source order (submit first), each keeping min-height size.control.min; block padding stays space.4.
responsive.desktop: From breakpoint.tablet the button row is inline: primary then secondary, space.3 gap, natural widths.

motion.hover: Background and border transitions at motion.duration.fast, motion.easing.standard, colors only — no layout shift.
motion.reduced: Inherited from the generated prefers-reduced-motion block; nothing here gates feedback on motion.

content.note: All copy is otherwise untouched — heading, consequence sentence, button labels and the refusal reason are behavior and stay verbatim.

acceptance: The page keeps the DT-0001 shell in all four page states: centred max-w-2xl column, space.5 padding, heading at type.size.xl and type.weight.medium
The consequence block uses color.consequence.subtle background and color.consequence.border border, and its role=alert survives
The problem banner uses color.danger.subtle background and color.danger.default border, opens with a semibold 'Refused:' prefix, and its role=alert survives
The problem banner and the consequence block are distinguishable with color vision deficiency: different border weights or the 'Refused:' prefix make the difference legible without hue
The refused state renders the reason in a notice block (color.notice.subtle / color.notice.border) with no form and nothing that looks disabled
The primary button remains accent-colored — nothing on this page is styled with color.danger except the problem banner
The secondary button visibly responds to hover: color.border.strong border and color.bg.sunken background
Both buttons keep a rendered min-height of exactly size.control.min (44px) at every viewport
On viewports under breakpoint.tablet the buttons are full-width and stacked with the submit first; from breakpoint.tablet they sit inline with space.3 gap
The platform's consequence sentence and refusal reasons render verbatim — no truncation or paraphrase at any width
No raw color, spacing, or size literal is introduced — every new value resolves to a token

references.value: Implement after DT-0003 — the min-height acceptance references size.control.min through the generated utility.

Buttons are styled via BUTTON_PRIMARY/BUTTON_SECONDARY in control.ts, shared product-wide; the hover/active additions land there and every confirmation page inherits them. The message-block roles are this page's markup.

Backlog: the-button-primitive-has-no-tokens (GitHub #108), second folded gap — first design ticket over a confirmation page. The pending-feedback gap found in the survey is NOT this ticket: it is behavior, filed as GitHub #153.
